transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-05-21 16:00 UTC — Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Ravi (Redwood SE), Jordan (CTO Saturn), Priya (Eng Mgr), Evan (SRE), Leah (Security)

Summary: Quick scoping session to align on workload portrait, define success criteria for a 4-week pilot, and agree benchmark plan to measure p95/p99 latency and unit cost. Customer has conversational and retrieval-augmented flows with heavy output token skew. They want a replay-based benchmark and a 2-hour live burst test.

[00:00] Alex (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining — i'm alex, i'm the AE on this. maya and ravi from infra will handle the benchmark side. quick round robin?
[00:18] Jordan (Saturn): jordan here — CTO, i'll be working with evan on the network bits and priya on the app side. small intro: we're ~200 engineers, main product does document Q&A + agent-style workflows.
[00:33] Priya: hi, priya. engineering manager on the conversational team. main constraints: latency for human-facing chat, cost for nightly batch indexing jobs.
[00:50] Maya (Redwood): great, thanks. goal for today is to capture qps shapes, token mix, and agree on bench methodology and success metrics. is that right alex?
[01:05] Alex: yes. also capture security checklist for private deployment possibility. leah?
[01:12] Leah (Saturn): yes, i'll want SOC2 artifacts, SSO/SAML details, KMS integration, and audit log retention options.
[01:28] Maya: noted. ok let's start with traffic. jordan, what does your typical qps and burst profile look like?
[01:36] Jordan: ok so baseline is about 12 qps sustained global, but we get regional spikes up to maybe 180 qps during product launches. most of our work is east coast/us-west, minimal apac for now.
[01:50] Priya: to add — the 180 is a very short burst, usually under 5 minutes. normal peak hour looks like 35-45 qps.
[02:02] Evan (SRE): concurrency wise, single request handles multiple downstream calls — so at our app layer concurrency is higher, we typically see 200-ish simultaneous open sessions but only 30 concurrent model inferences at steady state.
[02:17] Ravi (Redwood): that distinction is important — we size for model concurrency not app sessions. when you say 180 qps burst, is that single-token per request or long completion?
[02:28] Jordan: it's mixed. 60% are short clarifying prompts (input avg ~20 tokens, output avg ~60), 30% are retrieval-augmented longer answers (input avg ~120 tokens, output avg ~450), the remaining 10% are multi-step agent runs that can output 1k+ tokens.
[02:50] Maya: ok that's helpful. so token distribution is skewed — heavy long-tail. do you have percentiles? p95/p99 output token length?
[03:02] Priya: ballpark p95 output is ~600 tokens, p99 around 1.2k — but that's from our metrics which include agent aggregations, so might be slightly inflated vs raw model outputs.
[03:18] Alex: good. i'll write that down: avg input 40, avg output 150, p95 600, p99 1200 — we can refine with the sample.
[03:29] Jordan: yep, please treat those as approximate.
[03:34] Maya: next, latency targets — what does saturn need for SLOs?
[03:38] Priya: for interactive chat we want p95 under 750ms and p99 under 1.5s, but we can accept higher for long-form answers if we can show cost savings.
[03:51] Alex: interesting tradeoff — so you prefer hybrid: low latency for small responses, cost-optimized path for heavy outputs. that maps well to our routing options: single token low-latency model variant vs batched quantized model for bulk.
[04:07] Jordan: exactly. and we want automatic fallback if dedicated capacity is saturated — e.g., route to hosted lower-cost variant instead of failing.
[04:18] Maya: we'll propose a policy for routing by priority + length. ok on the benchmarking plan: we propose two phases — 1) replay of anonymized production traffic to measure p50/p95/p99 and token distribution; 2) synthetic burst windows to validate tail behavior and autoscaling.
[04:36] Ravi: replay should use preserved inter-arrival times if possible so we capture burstiness.
[04:42] Jordan: can you replay header-preserving? we can scrub PII.
[04:46] Maya: yes, we'll provide a replay harness. we'll need a 1M request sample that represents a 24-hour window ideally or a week compressed.
[04:56] Evan: small note — our network policy might block streaming websocket connections from unknown IPs; we'll need VPC peering or a jump-host.
[05:06] Alex: ok action item for evan to open a peering ticket and for us to provide endpoint IPs.
[05:12] Leah: on compliance — KMS/HSM integration is a blocker for private deployment. for hosted we'd want encryption-in-flight + field-level token redaction.
[05:23] Maya: we support KMS (customer-managed keys) and HSM tokens for private. for hosted we can offer envelope keys and audit logs. we'll share doc links.
[05:34] Priya: what's the expected cost delta if we choose dedicated reserved capacity vs hosted pay-as-you-go?
[05:41] Alex: rough rule: dedicated reserved is 30-50% cheaper for steady-state high qps and provides capacity guarantees. hosted is easier to start, but unit cost per token is higher. we will run exact numbers in the benchmark spreadsheet.
[05:57] Jordan: ok timeline?
[06:00] Alex: propose 4-week pilot: week 0 prep and data handoff, week 1 replay + baseline, week 2 optimization (batching/quantization tuning), week 3 burst validation and report.
[06:12] Priya: can we compress to 3 weeks? we have a product sprint in week 4.
[06:17] Maya: compress possible if customer provides traffic sample and we allow concurrent workstreams — but we should keep at least one full week for optimization. so 3-week compressed plan: 2 days prep, 5 days replay+baseline, 5 days tuning, final 3 days burst+deliverable.
[06:35] Jordan: let's aim for compressed. we can prioritize.
[06:38] Alex: noted. we'll tentatively plan compressed 3-week pilot starting 2027-05-31 pending sample.
[06:45] Evan: for the replay harness, what's the load-generator footprint? do you need us to provision load nodes in our VPC?
[06:51] Maya: we can run the generator from Redwood side but peered into your VPC for low-latency measurement. alternately, we can give you the dockerized generator to run inside your cluster.
[07:03] Priya: i'd prefer hosting inside our cluster — we can control network and avoid NAT issues.
[07:09] Ravi: cool. we'll provide docker image + instructions.
[07:12] Jordan: demo question — are you planning to use quantized models for heavy answers? will that affect hallucination rates?
[07:19] Maya: quantized models are a tradeoff. for many transformer families we see minimal quality degradation at 4-bit for decoding tasks, but for retrieval-augmented long answers we want to run evals against your prompt set. we'll include quality gating as part of success criteria.
[07:36] Alex: let's define the success criteria explicitly now. suggestions: p95 latency <=750ms for small responses (<=100 output tokens); end-to-end p95 within 20% of baseline for long answers with cost reduction >=20%; no regression in accuracy on 10 key prompts (we'll run automated eval).
[07:55] Priya: that seems fair. add: zero data exfil incidents and SOC2 artifacts reviewed.
[08:02] Leah: also need audit trail for admin actions and per-token logging options (redacted) for debug.
[08:11] Alex: okay we'll include audit log retention options and redaction guidance in the security pack.
[08:17] Jordan: how will you measure cost? is it per-token, per-request, or blended?
[08:22] Ravi: benchmark will produce cost-per-1k-output-tokens and cost-per-concurrent-session at different load levels. we'll break down GPU-hour and inference token costs.
[08:33] Priya: and can you show the impact of batching and prefix cache on latency/cost?
[08:38] Maya: yes — two tuning knobs: batching window and prefix/KV cache hit-rate. we'll instrument those and show modeled savings at observed cache-hit rates.
[08:49] Alex: any legal/procurement constraints?
[08:51] Jordan: procurement will require our standard MSA edits; timeline wise we need to sign by end of q2 if pricing is within our expectations.
[08:59] Alex: good to know.
[09:02] Evan: one operational question — what telemetry do we get to integrate with our monitoring (Datadog)?
[09:07] Maya: we export per-request traces, token-level counters, and model-level metrics via prometheus endpoints; we can provide a Grafana dashboard sample.
[09:17] Priya: do you support per-route quotas and throttles? we have some routes that must be prioritized.
[09:22] Alex: yes, per-route SLOs and rate-limits are supported in the runtime. we can show a demo during the pilot.
[09:30] Jordan: ok next steps recap?
[09:33] Alex: i'll read back: 1) redwood sends security pack + SOC2 snippets by 2027-05-24 — alex. 2) maya shares benchmark harness + docker by 2027-05-26. 3) saturn provides anonymized traffic sample (1M req or equivalent) by 2027-05-27 — jordan. 4) evan opens VPC peering ticket and shares network info. 5) schedule replay week of 2027-05-31. does that match?
[09:59] Jordan: yes.
[10:01] Leah: i will review security pack and come back with redlines.
[10:05] Priya: we'll confirm compressed 3-week pilot start if we get the sample.
[10:12] Alex: great. any final Qs?
[10:15] Jordan: just one — if the p99 is bad in replay, do you have autoscaling playbooks?
[10:21] Maya: yes — we have autoscale policies and fallback routing; we'll run a canary on canary models and failover to hosted variant if needed.
[10:30] Jordan: ok thanks everyone.
[10:33] Alex: thanks team, we'll follow up with materials.

End notes: Timeline tentative: compressed 3-week pilot starting 2027-05-31. Deliverables: benchmark report with p50/p95/p99 latency, token distribution histogram, cost per 1k tokens, tuning recommendations (batch/quantize/cache), security pack. Links referenced: benchmark spreadsheet (to be shared), replay harness repo (to be shared).

Transcript ends.
